notes: `לַמֶּלֶךְ` → *the king's* fuses the preposition with the noun that carries the genitive marker (rule 49's fused-genitive paragraph), the assimilated article taking the determiner standing before the possessor's word. The competing reading silences the `לְ` under rule 40; it is set aside because the possessive marker here is written on a word that would otherwise stand bare, so an English rendering is spent on the preposition's own relation.
The copula joins the nominal predicate `יוֹעֵץ` rather than the prepositional phrase modifying it (rules 20 and 49), discontinuous under rule 25.
